critical_finding.description: An establishment owner can, via a direct Supabase REST call with their own session JWT (bypassing the app's settings page entirely), overwrite registry-provenance columns (official_id, source_ministry, source_reference, source_url, source_updated_at, registry_import_batch) on their own establishment row. Confirmed real: base RLS policy is row-level only (no column restriction), and the only existing column-protection trigger (0014_rc1_security_fixes.sql) predates and does not cover these columns.
critical_finding.sprint_rule_invoked: REGISTRY-NATIONAL-D §28 — 'Si un chemin d'escalade réel existe : DECISION cannot be A.'

decision_reason: A real, currently-existing escalation path was found (owner can overwrite registry-provenance columns on their own establishment row via direct REST call — RLS is row-level only, no column protection covers these fields). Per the sprint's own §28 rule this means DECISION cannot be A, regardless of how clean the rest of the registry state is. A fix has been prepared (0023, not executed) but not applied — applying and verifying it is a prerequisite for true closure.
ready_for_cms_detail: Registry V1 data state is clean, reconciled, and fully documented (CMS boundary + handoff docs produced). CMS-A can safely begin schema/product planning using this handoff. It should NOT ship any NEW owner-editable establishments field, or any UI surface reading official_verification incorrectly, until the RLS/column-protection gap (0023 or equivalent) is reviewed and applied by Eddy/the architect.
